newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BOC sees vacuum orders pick up.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BOC sees vacuum orders pick up.

text.p: Health and industrial gases specialist BOC Group Plc said on Thursday that orders had begun to pick up at its vacuum business after it was hit hard by poor trading conditions in the semiconductor industry.

But in a telephone interview with Reuters following the publication of a two percent rise in first-quarter pre-tax group profit, chief executive Danny Rosenkranz said the vacuum appeared to have the worst behind it.
"It's always a difficult call, but my feeling is that the vacuum business is either at or near the bottom," he said.

While group pre-tax profit rose to 102.7 million stg from 100.8 million, operating profit in the vacuum business fell 13 percent to 12.1 million stg as expected following the collapse in the vacuum pump order book in the second half of 1996.
"(But) it is now on the way up," said Rosenkrantz, adding the positive order impact should offset the downward pressure stemming from sterling's strength.

"I would be disappointed if the year would finish sort of four times quarter one (operating profit)," he said. "If we move on into next year we should be on the way up and the year after that we should be flying," Rosenkrantz added.
At the moment order intake from the semi-conductor industry was about 50 to 60 percent from the levals seen a year ago.

Currency translations cost BOC five million stg in first-quarter profit and would hit full-year results by about 20 million if exchange rates stayed the same, financial director Tony Isaac said. But the pound's current strength was already discounted in analysts' full-year forecasts, he added.

"Most of the analysts' full-year figures are at around 445 to 450 million stg. We achieved 445 last year. The assumption is that we'll be there or there about after the impact of sterling," Isaac said. "That tends to show in the first quarter."
BOC's healthcare business saw operating profit retreat to 13.0 million stg from 13.5 million stg, but the results would have been unchanged if currency effects were excluded.
The business continued to suffer from lower prices for anaesthetic gas Forane, but Rosenkrantz repeated that results in the sector would be flat for the year as a whole.

"The currency made that assumption (of a flat result) a little bit tighter, but that is still what we're trying to do," added Rosenkrantz. In the core industrial gas business operating profits rose to 96.4 million stg from 94.1 million with higher results in Europe as well as the South Pacific and Asia.
"It is going very much as predicted. All parts of the world seem to be going well, particularly in Japan," said Rosenkrantz.
Speaking of the overall results, he said: "Things are going pretty well, although the currency is taking a little bit the shine off it."
